steps.notes: Passes ONLY with reverse-engineered interpretation: media n_total|n1|n2|n_total (n3 unused) AND the textbook formula l'=r+r*i'/u' that contradicts the prompt's eq (1)/(2). Literal-prompt impl and physical-doublet impl both FAIL.
Exact trace passes with the same hidden media mapping (air|n1|n2|air, n3 decoy), sinI1=h/r1, U1=0. Docstring is garbled (says 'paraxial' for the non-paraxial step).
Target encodes LC = l31(paraxial) - L31(marginal), positive; opposite of the standard LSA convention dL' = L' - l'. Standard-sign impl FAILS tests 0-3.

findings.evidence: The step background states, twice and self-consistently, a WRONG paraxial image-distance formula. Eq (1): "l' = (r*i)/u' + r" (uses i, the incidence angle) and the expanded eq (2): "l' = (l-r)/(1 + (l-r)/r - (n/n')*(l-r)/r) + r" (omits the n/n' factor in the numerator). The standard textbook relation, and the paraxial limit of the problem's own non-paraxial eq (5) ("L1' = R1 + R1*sin I1'/sin U1'"), is l' = r + r*i'/u' (refraction angle i'). The frozen target encodes the CORRECT textbook formula, not the prompt's: a literal implementation of eq (1)/(2) yields l31 = 26.7025 while the target is 80.27363883835613 (steptest official joint: FAIL, review/work/37/step_37.1_promptformula.py). The textbook-formula implementation matches the target to 1.1e-13 across all 3 tests (steptest: PASS, review/work/37/step_37.1.py). A solver who faithfully follows the explicitly given equations is scored wrong; passing requires recognizing the equations are erroneous and silently substituting the standard formula.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct eq (1) to l' = r*i'/u' + r and eq (2) to l' = (n/n')*(l-r)/(1 + (l-r)/r*(1 - n/n')) + r in the step background, matching the non-paraxial eq (5).

findings.evidence: The mapping of n1,n2,n3 onto the three refractions is never stated, and the target's choice is both unguessable and physically inconsistent with the prompt. Docstring: "n1/n2/n3 (float): Refractive index of the first/second/third lens material", "n_total: Refractive index of the surrounding medium (air)"; prompt says the system is a "doublet lens" (two materials). The target encodes media sequence n_total -> n1 -> n2 -> n_total (surface 3 exits from glass n2 back to air) with n3 COMPLETELY UNUSED: re-running the matching model with n3=9.99 still reproduces the D-light target bit-for-bit (review/work/37/verify_model.py: 'n3 decoy check ... True'). The two natural competing readings both fail: (a) literal three-material sequence air|n1|n2|n3 gives l31 = 231.17 (this is what GPT-5 implemented; SciCode/eval/inspect_ai/GPT5-90K_results/samples/37_epoch_1.json shows it scored 0/3 on this problem); (b) physical cemented-doublet air|n1|n3|air gives l31 = 99.575 (steptest FAIL, review/work/37/step_37.1_doublet.py). Target = 80.2736. Because the tests always call with n2 == n1 (e.g. 'calculate_paraxial(h1, ..., nD1, nD1, nD3, n)'), the system the targets describe is chromatically a thick SINGLET of crown glass; the flint indices nD3/nF3/nC3 defined in every test never affect the answer. This defect propagates identically to 37.2 and 37.3.
findings.suggested_fix: State the media sequence explicitly in the docstring/background (light travels n_total | n1 | n2 | n_total; surface k refracts from the medium before it into the medium after it; after the last surface the medium is n_total), and either remove n3 or regenerate targets from a true crown/flint doublet that actually uses it.

findings.evidence: Same hidden media mapping as 37.1, independently confirmed against the exact-trace targets: only n_total -> n1 -> n2 -> n_total with sinI1 = h1/r1, U1 = 0 reproduces all three 37.2 targets (max diff 1.4e-13; steptest PASS, review/work/37/step_37.2.py); n3 is again a decoy. A solver who failed to guess the mapping in 37.1 fails this independently-scored step as well (GPT-5's vector-Snell exact trace with media air|n1|n2|n3 was physically sound and scored 0).
findings.suggested_fix: Same as 37.1: document the media sequence and the parallel-ray initialization (object at infinity, sin I1 = h1/r1) explicitly.

findings.evidence: The sign/order of the difference is unstated and the problem's own labels point to the WRONG choice. Target encodes LC = l31(paraxial, step 1) - L31(marginal, step 2): t3[0][0] = 1.4326e-06 = t1[0][0] - t2[0][0] exactly, and LC is positive and increasing (test 3 asserts (LCC[0]<LCC[-1]) == True). The standard optics convention for longitudinal spherical aberration is deltaL' = L'(marginal) - l'(paraxial) (negative here); implementing that fails officially (steptest FAIL, review/work/37/step_37.3_stdsign.py — tests 0-2 sign-flipped arrays, test 3 boolean False vs True). Worse, the docstrings are internally swapped: 37.1's return is labeled "l31 ... Axial image locations" and 37.2's "L31 ... Paraxial image locations", so a solver who resolves the 37.3 docstring phrase "difference between paraxial and axial" via those labels computes L31 - l31 = the wrong sign. Only reading 'paraxial' as the true paraxial (step 1) result, against the step docstrings, passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Define LC explicitly in the 37.3 docstring as LC = l31_paraxial - L31_nonparaxial (positive for this undercorrected design), and fix the swapped 'Axial'/'Paraxial' return labels in 37.1/37.2.

findings.evidence: Garbled documentation throughout the step: the non-paraxial step's docstring opens "Computes the paraxial parameters for spherical aberration calculation" and labels the return "L31 ... Paraxial image locations"; the background opens "The paraxial optical path is calculated with assumption that the incident light is at angle >> 5 degree" (should be non-paraxial); the prompt lists inputs "light wavelength" and "grid scaling factor" that do not exist in the signature (wavelength enters only implicitly via the D/F/C index choice; no grid factor exists). Conversely 37.1's docstring labels the paraxial result "Axial image locations". These swapped labels are what arm the 37.3 sign trap.
findings.suggested_fix: Relabel: 37.1 returns 'paraxial image distance', 37.2 'marginal/non-paraxial image distance'; delete the nonexistent 'wavelength' and 'grid scaling factor' inputs from the prompts.

findings.evidence: Tests cannot detect mishandling of the second glass or of n3: every test calls with n2 == n1 (nD1,nD1 / nF1,nF1 / nC1,nC1) and the gold never uses n3, so an implementation that ignores BOTH n2 and n3 (hard-coding media air|n1|n1|air) passes officially (steptest PASS, review/work/37/step_37.1_ignore_n2n3.py). The same holds for 37.2/37.3. Surface 2 is a numeric no-op in every test, so its refraction code path is never exercised.
findings.suggested_fix: Add at least one test case with n2 != n1 (a real crown/flint pair at the cemented interface) after fixing the media-mapping spec, so the second refraction and the n3 parameter are actually constrained.

overall_assessment: Not fair to score as-is. All three steps pass only under a conjunction of three author idiosyncrasies that the prompt either omits or actively contradicts: (1) the background's paraxial equations (1)/(2) are wrong optics (i instead of i') and must be silently overridden with the textbook formula; (2) the index-to-surface mapping is unstated, the target's choice (air|n1|n2|air) leaves the documented 'third lens material' n3 a pure decoy, and the two natural readings (literal air|n1|n2|n3, physical doublet air|n1|n3|air) both fail; (3) the aberration sign is the reverse of the standard LSA convention and the swapped 'Axial'/'Paraxial' docstring labels point to the wrong order. GPT-5's physically competent 0/3 on this problem (bundled results file) is direct evidence the defects mis-score strong solvers. Fixable by correcting eq (1)/(2), documenting the media sequence, fixing the swapped labels, and defining LC's sign explicitly.
